propositions.claim: The held text is a GPO slip-order printing of EO 6730 dated May 30, 1934.
The order approves the amendments to the Code.
propositions.quote: do hereby order that said amendments to said Code be, and they hereby are , approved

propositions.claim: The order approves the Code as amended, effective June 11, 1934.
propositions.quote: said Code as amended by said amendments , a copy of which is hereto attached as Exhibit B, be and it hereby is approved

propositions.claim: The continuation of the 1933 Code ran only until the effective date, June 11, 1934, by the order's own terms. This ends the continuation clause only, not every provision of the earlier Code independently.
propositions.quote: to become effective on June 11 , 1934, prior to which effective date the Code of Fair Competition approved August 19 , 1933 , shall con­tinue in full force and effect

propositions.claim: Statement 1 recites a direction already given for a joint study, with a six-month report requested. It does not show that the study was performed or the direction ended.
propositions.quote: I have directed the Federal Trade Commission and the National Recovery Administration to study further and jointly the operation of the basing point system

propositions.claim: Statement 2 is a presidential undertaking on employee elections, qualified by 'as the occasion may demand'. It does not show that any election was held.
propositions.quote: I will undertake promptly to provide , as the occasion may demand , for the election by employees in each indus­trial unit of representatives of their own choosing

propositions.claim: The joint resolution of June 14, 1935 (ch. 246, sec. 2) repealed the Title I provisions letting the President approve codes and providing for their enforcement; it names no code or order.
propositions.quote: All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed

propositions.claim: Section 1 of the same resolution substituted 'on April 1, 1936' for the two-year phrase in section 2 (c) of Title I. This shows the amendment only, not that every Title I provision or EO 6730 expired on that date.
propositions.quote: section 2 (c) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act is amended by striking out "at the expiration of two years after the date of enactment of this Act" and inserting in lieu thereof "on April 1, 1936"

propositions.claim: The order also adopts and approves the Administrator's report, recommendations and findings, a distinct approval from the approval of the amendments and of the amended Code.
propositions.quote: do adopt and approve the report, recommendations and findings of the Administrator

propositions.claim: The repeal in sec. 2 of the June 14, 1935 resolution carries a proviso keeping the section 5 exemption for two specified kinds of agreements and action under them, so the repeal sentence alone is not a complete closure of Title I effects. The proviso does not name EO 6730 or any code and does not show current operation.
propositions.quote: Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder (1) putting into effect the requirements of section 7 (a), including minimum wages, maximum hours, and prohibition of child labor; and (2) prohibiting unfair competitive practices which offend against existing law

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN follows the project rule requiring a named ending or another qualifying termination basis: the verified general repeal does not name this order, and the study and election provisions remain unresolved. The fixed-date continuation alone ended under its own terms. Formal status is upheld only as the limited statement that no express ending was found in the checked evidence, not proof that none exists. The basis is the project's OPEN fallback despite the worker's uninformative 'none' label.
missed_evidence: The held photius original additionally says 'do adopt and approve the report, recommendations and findings of the Administrator.' The clause inventory omits this distinct approval and gives it no state, preventing T4.

49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, section 2 retains a qualified section 5 exemption through a proviso covering specified agreements and actions. This directly matters to the stated savings/residuals gap and prevents treating the repeal sentence alone as complete closure; it does not establish current operation.
review.stop_code_verdict: confirmed — for the first gap's narrow request for an owner ruling on class-wide termination. The slice labels the class 'swept' but supplies no class doctrine or named ending instrument. That label is only a lead; NEEDS_RULING does not excuse the separate uncompleted documentary checks.

verdicts.reason: Opened both held files. The photius printing identifies EO 6730 and May 30, 1934; the corroborating mabillon printing bears the GPO imprint and the reported date OCR error.
The held original contains the quoted approval of the amendments.
The held original approves the amended Code and immediately specifies June 11, 1934 as its effective date.
The original expressly limits this continuation to the period before the fixed June 11, 1934 effective date. This ends that continuation clause, not every provision of the earlier Code independently.
The original recites the joint FTC/NRA study direction and subsequently requests results within six months. It does not establish performance or termination.
The quoted undertaking appears in the original, qualified by 'as the occasion may demand.' It does not establish that elections occurred.

Read the same statutory page at https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-49/pdf/STATUTE-49-Pg375.pdf. Chapter 246, section 2 contains the quoted repeal and names neither EO 6730 nor an individual code.
Chapter 246, section 1 substitutes 'on April 1, 1936' for the quoted two-year phrase. This confirms the amendment, but not an independent finding that every Title I provision or EO 6730 expired then.
The cited CustomsMobile note and its section-page alternative were inaccessible; a direct retrieval also failed. The quotation and surrounding constitutional-history claim could not be confirmed.
